title: Localization of pSYN Aggregates in Axons or Dendrites
author: Andrew D Sauerbeck

steps.title: Load required Python packages
steps.instruction: Import all Python packages listed in the provided code before any analysis.

steps.title: Define experiment input parameters
steps.instruction: Specify the image file location, the folder for saving output images, the folder for saving copies of pre‑processed images, and the naming suffix to be appended to saved files.

steps.title: Prepare verified binarized masks
steps.instruction: Generate binarized masks for each image manually, verify their accuracy, and ensure they are available before running the analysis code.

steps.title: Set fixed intensity cutoff for tilescans
steps.instruction: For tilescan images, choose a fixed intensity cutoff that will be applied uniformly across all tiles to identify positive aggregate labeling.

steps.title: Correct chromatic aberration
steps.instruction: Measure and correct chromatic aberration using Channel Alignment images.

substeps.instruction: Select the brightest puncta in the images and use the top 5 % as the reference set.
Specify which channel in the raw image is the reference channel.
Specify the channel(s) that must be aligned to the reference channel.
If imaging three channels, choose the fluorophore with the most central wavelength as the reference to minimise cropping effects.
Enter the system‑ and objective‑specific alignment values required for correction.

steps.title: Configure colocalization analysis parameters
steps.instruction: Set the parameters that control how colocalization is evaluated.

substeps.instruction: Set **mask_type** to either **'positive'** (use the entire binarized mask) or **'negative'** (exclude voxels that overlap the mask from the other channel/type).
Set **selection_type** to **'pure'**, **'any'**, or **'percent'**; **'percent'** is recommended because it provides high confidence without being overly restrictive.

steps.title: Specify raw image size for tiling
steps.instruction: Define the dimensions of the raw acquired Airyscan image so the mosaic tiling key can be correctly adjusted after post‑acquisition processing.

steps.title: Provide remaining Z‑slice count
steps.instruction: Enter the number of optical Z‑slices that remain in the dataset after chromatic‑aberration correction.

steps.title: Build mosaic tiling key
steps.instruction: Run the provided code block that loads required processing definitions and constructs the mosaic tiling key.

steps.title: Process or load preprocessed images
steps.instruction: Execute the appropriate code block depending on whether the image has been processed before.

substeps.instruction: If the image has not been processed, run the preprocessing code block.
If a previously processed image and its output are already saved, skip the preprocessing block.
If you are loading previously saved pre‑processed images, run the reload‑data block.

steps.title: Run colocalization analysis
steps.instruction: Execute the colocalization analysis code block, defining only the optical sections that will be used to generate the output maximum‑intensity projections.

steps.title: Organize colocalization results
steps.instruction: Run the data‑organization block to prepare results for manual export.

substeps.instruction: After execution, the variable **all_organized_data_by_tile** contains the aggregated counts.
Column 2 holds the number of aggregates colocalized with dendrites; column 3 holds the number colocalized with axons.
Each row corresponds to a single imaging tile.

steps.title: Perform randomization analysis (optional)
steps.instruction: If desired, run the provided randomization code block to model colocalization outcomes under conditions of random chance.
